title: Add token-ladder and cumulative-stitch metrics for SLO root-cause
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We currently expose token-level cost and phase breakdown metrics, but teams still struggle to quickly identify SLO regressions caused by subtle per-token shifts across stages (tokenization, attention kernels, kv fetch, postprocessing). This PR introduces two complementary observability primitives: 1) token-ladder metrics — a compact, incremental per-token latency/cost series that shows delta contribution at each token position and stage; 2) cumulative-stitch rollups — lightweight cumulative aggregates that stitch token-ladder samples into session-level and route-level time-series for alerting and dashboards. Motivation: incident postmortems (ENG-2124) show long-tail SLO regressions where total latency increased without a clear single-stage spike. Token-ladder makes the per-token incremental contribution visible; cumulative-stitch provides an efficient rollup for long-term alerting without exploding cardinality. Changes: - New metrics: telemetry.token_ladder{tenant,route,model,stage,token_offset} (histogram), telemetry.cumulative_stitch{tenant,route,model,window} (sum/counter). - Sampling policy: token-ladder is sampled at 1:200 by default with deterministic seeding per invocation to preserve relative ordering across retries. - Aggregation: stitch rollups compute prefix sums over token-ladder for configurable windows (30s/5m/1h) and expose derived percentiles used by alerts. - Dashboard: added a Token Ladder panel (compact sparklines with stage stacks) and a Cumulative Stitch heatmap for routes. - Alerts: new alert rule slo.token_stitch_regression triggers when 95th percentile cumulative-stitch latency increases by >20% vs baseline over 6h with minimum sample floor. This PR includes an auto-mute for low-volume routes to reduce noise. Checklist: - [x] implement metric emission hooks in runtime stage manager - [x] implement sampling policy and deterministic seeding - [x] add stitch aggregation job with rollup retention - [x] create Grafana panels and dashboard JSON - [x] add alert and runbook - [x] unit tests for metric tagging and sampling - [x] integration sanity run on staging Testing: Unit + integration tests included. Staging playback ran a synthetic traffic mix (see commit msgs) and validated that token-ladder captures an introduced KV fetch jitter with the expected per-token delta at offsets 6..9. We also exercised the cumulative-stitch alert by simulating a controlled 25% increase in kernel latency; alert fired and auto-mute prevented noise for low-volume tenants. Rollout plan: - Feature gated behind observability.experimental.token_ladder flag - Enable for beta tenants for 2 weeks, monitor alert churn - Gradually enable default sampling for all hosted accounts after stabilization Release notes: - Added token-ladder and cumulative-stitch telemetry for improved per-token SLO root-cause analysis - New Grafana dashboard panels and an alert rule (slo.token_stitch_regression) - Experimental feature behind feature flag Backwards compatibility / cost: Default sampling keeps cardinality increases small. Stitch rollups are retained at coarse resolution to limit storage. Ops runbook summary included in repo/docs/observability/runbooks/token-ladder.md (linked).

review_comments: Diego Ramos (2026-02-16): Nice work. A few asks: 1) please document the sampling seed determinism and how it behaves across retries/redirects; 2) consider lowering default sampling for extremely high-throughput models.
Asha Patel (2026-02-16): Responded: added seeding details in seeding_util.go comments and added a config override for per-model sampling rates. Also added a note in the runbook about retry semantics.
Maya Chen (2026-02-17): Question on alert noise — what's the expected false positive rate during model rollout windows? Can we auto-suppress around canary rollouts?
Asha Patel (2026-02-17): Answered: added auto-mute logic when Linear tag 'rollout=true' is present on routes; added sample floor requirement to alert to avoid triggering on very low volumes.
Diego Ramos (2026-02-18): Approved after minor nits fixed in dashboard legends and unit test flakiness addressed.
